findings.detail: For three ticks I described the held po rows as 'bounded by PO's next triage pass', citing last_triaged_at 2026-08-24T07:37:00Z as proof of a live consumer. Measured the consumer's actual dispatch path this tick and the framing does not survive it. Across ALL THREE session-armed cron families: cowork-team 0 references to the po agent, cron-detect-loop 0 (its register.md dispatches only docs/agents/dev-team/ and docs/agents/system-auditor/), cron-standalone-team 0 — its single grep hit is the substring inside the word 'repo'. cowork-schedule.json has 0 slots whose agent or slot_id matches po. So PO is reachable ONLY by router hand-dispatch, by an agent chaining next_agent:po, or from inside the dev-team flow. The 07:37Z triage was one of those unscheduled events, not a cadence.
findings.impact: 'Bounded by PO's next pass' is bounded by an event nothing schedules. The 7 held rows (1 HIGH bctc_image_fetch_degraded now ~1h45m old, 6 MED CCATO) have no arrival time. This is the same shape as the qa-responder finding — an agent that looks alive because it recently ran, while its only live path is demand-driven or manual — except qa-responder's path was INTACT in source and PO's is genuinely absent from every armed schedule.
findings.fix: Router is hand-dispatching po after this tick body completes, as a distinct action outside the dispatcher (match-slots.md:115's spawn-guard forbids the cowork dispatcher itself from spawning dev-team agents). The durable fix is a product decision: give po a cron cadence, or accept manual-only and make the drain's escalation path explicit rather than 'log for PO'.
